Subject: Private fleet upgrade: snapshot rollback approach (FinEdge)

Hi Avery,

Were mapping out the July maintenance window for our private deployment with Redwood (FinEdges private cluster). Our network team prefers snapshot-first rollback rather than full-version unpin + redeploy because we have complex routing and stateful LVM volumes.

High-level asks:
- Can Redwood provide a snapshot-based rollback playbook that minimizes service disruption (prefer read-only fallback vs full rollback)?
- We need explicit steps for: filesystem snapshot, model-serving container snapshot, KV cache invalidation, and DB schema compatibility checks.
- What are the expected downtime and SLAs for a snapshot rollback vs a full unpin rollback?

Were aiming for the maintenance window: 2026-07-30 02:00-04:00 UTC. If you have a rehearsal runbook we can use in our staging environment that would help.

Thanks,
Samir

Subject: Re: Private fleet upgrade: snapshot rollback approach (FinEdge)

Samir,

Thanks for the details and the window. Ive attached a first-draft playbook (redwood-snapshot-rollback-playbook-v1.pdf) and a concise preflight checklist (private-upgrade-preflight-checklist.csv). Key points up-front:

- Snapshot-first approach: we recommend taking storage-level snapshots (LVM/ZFS) + container filesystem snapshot (if using overlayfs) before any config or binary updates. This allows an atomic switch back with minimal orchestration.
- Read-only fallback: where possible well prefer a staged fallback (route traffic to read-only endpoints + pause write-critical paths) to avoid full rollback. Full rollback is the fallback if read-only leaves unacceptable consistency hazards.
- KV cache considerations: in-memory caches (redis/memcached) will need either a coordinated flush or a warming plan; we include a warming script in the playbook that rehydrates from persistent backing store.
- Version pinning: pin the model-serving symlink to the release dir (e.g., /opt/redwood/model-vX.Y.Z -> active). Rollback can be as fast as flipping the symlink and restarting the container if underlying binary compatibility is guaranteed.

Immediate open items for you:
1) Confirm snapshot retention policy (how many snapshots we keep and retention TTL)
2) Confirm whether youre using block-level snapshots (LVM/zfs) or VM-level snapshots (vSphere/OpenStack)
3) Provide a contact from NetOps who can be on the bridge for the rehearsal and the production window

Proposed rehearsal: 2026-07-27 10:00-11:30 UTC in your staging cluster. Well run the playbook end-to-end and validate rollback time and data integrity checks.

Ive CCd Karthik for runtime specifics and Soojin/Neha for change approvals and compliance hooks.

Best,
Avery

Folks,

Two technical notes from the runtime side (to complement Averys playbook):

- Kernel and driver compatibility: if the upgrade touches the GPU driver stack (CUDA/NVIDIA) or kernel modules, snapshot rollback at the application level (symlink flip) may not be sufficient. For on-prem nodes that require driver changes we recommend: snapshot VM image (or host-level snapshot), perform driver upgrade on a single canary host, validate, then proceed.

- KV cache invalidation pattern: use a two-step approach
  1) mark cache read-only (clients tolerate stale reads for 30s)
  2) atomically swap cache namespace and warm the new namespace from persistent store.

- Fast rollback commands (example):
  # switch model dir back
  sudo ln -sfn /opt/redwood/model-v2.4.1 /opt/redwood/active-model
  docker restart redwood-model-server

  # re-enable traffic after health checks pass
  curl -sSf http://localhost:8080/health || exit 1

- Expected RTO: for a purely application-level rollback (symlink + container restart) were typically ~90-180s assuming the model weights are already present on disk and KV warming is fast. For driver or kernel level rollback (host repaint), expect 20-45m per host depending on autoscaling and how quickly traffic can be drained.

- Telemetry and checkpoints: please ensure your snapshot metadata includes a UUID and timestamp we can reference in the after-action report (playbook includes a sample tagging schema).

Ill bring a small script to the rehearsal that automates the symlink flip + healthcheck gating. If FinEdge wants a more conservative fallback, we can route writes to a staging shard for the 10-15 minute window while verifying end-to-end consistency.

-Karthik
